frame.source: Home Office police recorded crime · author's analysis

definitions.total: Every notifiable offence recorded by the 43 police forces of England and Wales. Excludes fraud, which is recorded centrally by Action Fraud rather than by any force, and British Transport Police, which polices no resident population.
definitions.violence: Offences against the person, from harassment through to homicide. Heavily affected by changes in how forces record what is reported to them, so long-run comparisons need care.
definitions.vio_noinj: Assault that caused no physical injury, plus threats, and offences such as modern slavery. Recording practice for these offences tightened after 2014, so the series is not directly comparable across that point.
definitions.vio_inj: Assault where the victim was physically hurt, from actual bodily harm up to grievous bodily harm with intent.
definitions.stalking: Stalking, harassment, malicious communications, and controlling or coercive behaviour. The Home Office only separated these out in 2013/14; earlier years are shown on the same basis so the series reads continuously.
definitions.driving_death: Causing death or serious injury by driving: dangerous, careless, unlicensed, or under the influence.
definitions.homicide: Murder, manslaughter, corporate manslaughter, and infanticide. Counted per victim, so one incident can record more than one.
definitions.modern_slavery: Holding a person in slavery or servitude, or arranging their travel for exploitation. Its own offence only from 2015/16.
definitions.theft: All theft, from shoplifting to burglary and vehicle crime. The largest offence group: about half of all recorded crime.
definitions.other_theft: Theft that fits none of the named categories - theft in a dwelling, theft of mail, theft by an employee, making off without payment, and blackmail.
definitions.tfp: Theft directly from a person without force: pickpocketing, bag-dipping, and snatches the victim does not resist. If force or the threat of it is used, it is robbery instead.
definitions.shoplifting: Theft from a shop or stall.
definitions.vehicle: Vehicles as targets of theft: theft of them, theft from them, and interfering with them. Not driving offences, and not damage - the Home Office counts those elsewhere, and they are shown here only as related views.
definitions.veh_from: Theft of property from inside or attached to a vehicle - the largest single vehicle offence.
definitions.veh_of: Theft or unauthorised taking of a motor vehicle, including aggravated vehicle taking.
definitions.veh_interfere: Tampering with a vehicle or its parts with intent to steal - caught before a theft was completed.
definitions.burglary: Entering a building as a trespasser to steal, or to commit certain other offences. Split by whether the building is somebody's home.
definitions.burg_homes: Burglary of a dwelling. Called domestic burglary before 2017 and residential burglary after; the same offences, summed across the rename.
definitions.burg_other: Burglary of a building that is not a home - shops, offices, sheds, and garages.
definitions.robbery: Theft using force or the threat of force. A phone taken after a struggle is robbery; a pocket picked unnoticed is theft from the person.
definitions.rob_personal: Robbery of an individual's own property, in the street or anywhere else.
definitions.rob_business: Robbery of property belonging to a business - a till, a delivery, a shop's takings.
definitions.sexual: All sexual offences, from exposure and voyeurism through to rape.
definitions.rape: Rape and attempted rape, of adults and of children.
definitions.sex_assault: Sexual touching without consent. Counted separately by the Home Office for male and female victims and for children under 13, and shown here as one figure.
definitions.exposure: Indecent exposure, and voyeurism - observing or recording someone doing a private act without their consent.
definitions.child_sexual: Grooming, sexual activity with a child, abuse of a position of trust, and abuse of children through prostitution or pornography. Sexual assault of a child is counted under sexual assault, not here.
definitions.other_sexual: What is left of the sexual offences group - causing sexual activity without consent, offences against a person with a mental disorder, familial sexual offences, and other miscellaneous sexual offences.
definitions.damage: Destroying or damaging property, including by fire.
definitions.dam_criminal: Damaging or destroying property without fire.
definitions.dam_arson: Damaging or destroying property by fire, whether or not life was endangered.
definitions.dam_vehicle: Damaging a vehicle without taking it - keyed panels, smashed windows, and slashed tyres.
definitions.threat_damage: Threatening to damage property, or having something with you intending to.
definitions.drugs: Possession, supply, and production of controlled drugs.
definitions.drug_poss: Possession of a controlled drug for personal use.
definitions.drug_traf: Supplying or producing controlled drugs, or possessing them with intent to supply.
definitions.order: Offences that disturb public order, from causing alarm or distress up to violent disorder.
definitions.order_fad: Causing fear, alarm or distress. The Home Office does not separate the Public Order Act sections here, so affray, threatening behaviour, and section 5 harassment, alarm, or distress all sit inside this one figure.
definitions.order_racial: Causing fear, alarm, or distress where racial or religious hostility was demonstrated or provided the motive. The main route by which hate speech, online and off, reaches the figures. Assaults, harassment, and criminal damage have their own racially aggravated offences, counted in those categories rather than here.
definitions.order_disorder: Violent disorder: twelve or more people using or threatening unlawful violence. Riot is a separate offence but records no counts in this series.
definitions.order_other: A single Home Office code - other offences against the State or public order - covering whatever the other three do not. It cannot be broken down any further here. Riot and treason have codes of their own but record no offences in this series.
definitions.weapons: Carrying a weapon, not using one - an offence in itself, whatever else did or did not happen.
definitions.wep_blade: Having an article with a blade or point in a public place or a school.
definitions.wep_firearms: Possession of a firearm, with or without intent to use it.
definitions.wep_other: Possession of an offensive weapon that is neither a firearm nor a blade.
definitions.misc: The Home Office's catch-all: 36 offence codes that fit nowhere else, from obscene publications to perjury.
definitions.obscene: Publishing, distributing, or possessing obscene material.
definitions.handling: Receiving, keeping, or selling goods known or believed to be stolen.
definitions.dangerous_driving: Dangerous driving that did not cause death or serious injury.
definitions.going_equipped: Being caught with tools intended for a theft or burglary that had not yet happened.
definitions.soliciting: Soliciting or loitering for the purposes of prostitution.
definitions.exploitation: Causing, inciting, or controlling prostitution for gain.
definitions.other_misc: The rest of the miscellaneous group - perjury, bail offences, forgery, wildlife offences, and numerous other hard-to-categorise offences.
definitions.knife: Selected serious offences where a knife or sharp instrument was used or threatened. It incorporates offences from the other categories rather than sitting beside them: every offence here is also counted in its own crime type, so knife robbery is part of robbery and homicide with a knife is part of homicide. A separate Home Office collection, which is why it reaches back to 2008/09 when the rest starts in 2012/13.
definitions.knife_robbery: Robbery where a knife was used or threatened. About a quarter of all London robbery.
definitions.knife_assault: Assault causing injury, or with intent to cause serious harm, where a knife was used or threatened.
definitions.knife_threats: Threats to kill involving a knife.
definitions.knife_rape: Rape where a knife was used or threatened.
definitions.knife_sexassault: Sexual assault where a knife was used or threatened.
definitions.knife_homicide: Homicide where a knife or sharp instrument was used - close to half of all London homicide.

notes.rate: Rate per 1,000 residents. ONS has published no police-force-area population estimate beyond mid-2024; later periods carry that figure forward and are shown paler.
notes.recency: Home Office revises the whole series at each quarterly release, so earlier periods can change slightly too.
notes.index: Indexed to the first period shown = 100.
notes.nesting: Some categories are contained in others — homicide, violence with injury and stalking are part of violence against the person; rape is part of sexual offences. They are shown one at a time and are not meant to be added together.

meta.population_source: ONS population estimates for police force areas, mid-1991 to mid-2024 (released 18 Dec 2025)

data_quality_notes.notes: GMP stopped submitting data after June 2019 due to failures in the PoliceWorks record management system installed in 2019. HMICFRS placed GMP in special measures in 2020 after discovering 80,000+ crimes had gone unrecorded. As of 2024 the system remains in use. Only 14 records exist for Aug 2022; no data from Jul 2019 onward. This is Englands 2nd largest force (~30k crimes/month when reporting). GMP local neighbourhood crime data (6 categories only) has been loaded into gmp_neighbourhood_crime table for this period.

Home Office knife data from April 2019 uses the NDQIS methodology for identifying knife/sharp-instrument involvement. Pre-Apr-2019 data was revised for coverage but the Home Office still states the series is NOT directly comparable across this break.

Fraud is recorded centrally - Action Fraud, CIFAS, UK Finance and Financial Fraud Action UK (force_kind='central', canonical force IS NULL) - not by territorial forces, and those bodies report on a longer lag than the 43. In the 2026-07-23 release the last fraud quarter is Jul-Sep 2025, so the two most recent quarters (Oct-Dec 2025 and Jan-Mar 2026) carry NO fraud at all. Fraud runs ~330k offences a quarter, about a fifth of the total: summing ho_recorded_crime across all forces reads 1,247,489 for Q4 2025/26 against 1,579,956 for Q4 2024/25, a 21% 'fall' that is entirely the absent collection - every territorial force is between -10% and +1.5% year on year over the same pair. Expect it to be backfilled in a later quarterly release; treat the newest two quarters of any release the same way. NOTHING IN THE DATA ANNOUNCES THIS: all 43 forces are present, and ~1.25m is a believable quarterly total, so the drop looks like news. Anything filtering force_kind='territorial' is unaffected and excludes fraud by construction - which is what london_crime_charts does.
GMP data for Jan-Jun 2019 may be affected by early PoliceWorks issues. Crime counts are broadly consistent with 2018 levels but recording accuracy is uncertain.
GMP reviewed its knife recording in Dec 2017 and found it had been under-counting. Sharp increase through 2018; earlier data NOT revised, so GMP knife figures are not comparable across that boundary.

Gwent filed no street-level data for the 8 months Sep 2025 - Apr 2026; reporting resumes May 2026. Unlike a reporting lag this is a hole in the middle of the series, so any period overlapping it undercounts England & Wales totals. Found by the london_crime_charts coverage check, where it pushed the 12-months-to-May-2026 anti-social-behaviour bar over the 2% shortfall line and caused that period to be excluded. Gwent is ~1.1% of the England & Wales population.

The Met filed every month, but roughly 5-7% of its recorded crime did not reach the published street-level extract for Mar - Aug 2024. Measured against two independent sources that agree: Home Office recorded crime, and the Met's own M1045 dashboard, against which police.uk falls from 98-99% to 92.7-94.9% across these months and recovers from Sep 2024. The dashboard shows no dip at all, so the crimes were recorded - they were not published. From Feb 2024 the count of Met records published with a blank LSOA drops from 0.7-7% to exactly zero, which is consistent with records whose location could not be resolved being withheld rather than published unlocated; control forces do not change. Loss is heaviest for victim-reported property crime (vehicle -7.5pp, theft -7.0pp) and nil for the officer-generated categories (public order -0.6pp, weapons -0.4pp). Believed to be a second artefact of the Met's CONNECT record management system change, whose known effect was to improve borough and degrade ward allocation from Mar 2024. A gap detector CANNOT see this: the force filed every month. Anything using police.uk London data over this window understates it; work built on met_dashboard is unaffected. Note also a separate, unexplained London deficit that begins in 2019 and never fully closes.

MPS reviewed its knife/sharp-instrument recording from April 2024, finding over-counting for some crime types and under-counting for others. Records corrected from Apr 2024; earlier data NOT revised, so ho_recorded_crime source='knife' is not directly comparable across that boundary. This is the main cause of the residual gap between the MPS and Home Office knife series.

mps_knife_outcomes.month is the month the OUTCOME WAS ACHIEVED, not the month of the offence. Outcomes are not backdated, so most rows attach to offences recorded in earlier months and a per-month outcome rate computed against mps_knife_offences is invalid. Outcome counts are also sensitive to administrative processing - the MPS attributes the Jan 2026 peak to backlog clearance, not to investigative performance.
Single month of missing data (Jun 2022). City of London is a small force; minor impact.
3 months of missing data (Nov 2022 - Jan 2023). Cause unknown.

POSITIVE note, recorded so it is not mistaken for a break: the MPS applies the LATEST Home Office definition to all current and historic data in this publication, so mps_knife_* trends are NOT driven by definition changes. This is the opposite of ho_recorded_crime source='knife', which carries the Apr 2019 NDQIS break and the Apr 2012 offence-code change. It is also why the MPS runs 2-7% above the Home Office before 2020: the MPS restates history on today's definition, the Home Office publishes what was submitted at the time.

The Home Office publishes knife data in three separate worksheets - 2008-09_to_2009-10, 2010-11_to_2011-12, 2012-13-onwards - BECAUSE they are not directly comparable (West Midlands recording change Apr 2010; offence code changes Apr 2012). ho_recorded_crime flattens all three into one continuous series with nothing marking the joins.
BTP has no street crime data for 12 months (Feb 2016 - Jan 2017). Cause unknown.
BTP has no street crime data from Feb 2025 onward. May be a reporting lag or system issue.

Last filed Jan 2026; no street-level data Feb 2026 onward as at the Jul 2026 ingest. Consistent with reporting lag rather than a system failure, but it compounds with the Gwent gap in any recent 12-month window. Gloucestershire is ~1.0% of the England & Wales population.

In mps_knife_offences the non-Total breakdowns do NOT partition the offence total - they are overlapping attributes, because an offence can be knife-used-to-injure AND domestic-abuse-flagged AND severe. The three Knife Used to... rows alone overrun the total by 0.7%; summing all five non-Total breakdowns overshoots it by 15% (workbook Note 1). Only breakdown='Total' is additive.

Migrating the MPS crime recording system to the cloud made the NDQIS review run more consistently, so offences previously missed or delayed in review are now identified. The MPS states this raised recorded knife crime by 1.2% between Apr 2025 and Feb 2026 - improved completeness, NOT a change in underlying levels. Source: MPS knife-enabled crime bulletin, Jun 2026.

The MPS crime recording system changed from CRIS to CONNECT in early 2024 - the workbook's Notes sheet says March 2024, the quarterly bulletin says February 2024. The MPS states counting methodologies changed for some categories relevant to knife crime - domestic abuse specifically - and that CONNECT-to-CRIS comparisons should be made with caution. Affects the Flagged As Domestic Abuse breakdown either side of that date. CONNECT also brought the injury-type field (workbook Note 17), which is why Severe or Fatal Injury is blank before Apr 2024.

met_dashboard's Dec 2025 knife slice is under-populated. It reads 929 offences against 1,116 in Nov and 1,088 in Jan. For Oct-Dec 2025 met_dashboard totals 3,233 where mps_knife_offences gives 3,364 and the independent Home Office knife collection gives 3,390 - so the MPS knife tables are within 0.77% of the Home Office and met_dashboard is 4.6% below it. Prefer mps_knife_offences for that month. Found 2026-08 while building the MPS knife ingest; cause not established, most likely a partial slice taken wholesale under met_dashboard's slice-level supersession.
